name: Rooftop Garden Cart
description: A small electric cart designed to operate exclusively on rooftop surfaces, moving between the urban farms and garden plots that cover the tops of Shelf tower blocks. The carts haul soil, water, tools, and harvested produce across rooftop landscapes connected by improvised ramps and bridges. They never touch street level. An entire agricultural economy operates above the city, and the Garden Carts are its trucks — small, quiet, solar-charged, and built by people who grow food on concrete because the alternative is not eating.
propulsion: Electric, solar-charged, small wheels for rooftop surfaces
range: 8 km per charge (solar extends indefinitely in daylight)
common_usage: Rooftop agriculture logistics, produce distribution, soil and water transport, community farming.
story_hooks: The rooftop garden network maps to an aerial view that spells out a message visible only from the executive zeppelins above — the farmers know exactly who's watching
A Garden Cart operator discovers that the soil they've been hauling contains trace elements that don't exist in any known geological survey — someone is seeding the rooftop farms with something
